characters.name: Rail Steward Essi
characters.role: Keeper of the bell rail and repair docket

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: The loading shutter has a narrow opening before the bell. One watch has to tell people when to be ready. The draft says a match at a glance is enough. Check the two records in the Letter Gallery, and bring the repair seal and rail record to the watch.

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: The clock starts at twelve in each practice case. Compare its first reading to the separate drum. Then advance the trial one minute. See what can happen in a case that agrees at the start.

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: In two cases the first readings agreed. Only one watch moved on the next minute. The third watch showed twelve against an eleven reading and stayed there. Someone could agree about the time at that first glance and still have a watch that cannot carry them through the shift.

dialogue.speaker: council-keeper
dialogue.text: I can sign a record of a test I made. The stamp has that test’s date. The shift crew keeps a way to compare the watch again when the record grows old.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Look for a source that tells you how someone checked a claim. The old optics note records a way of testing. The Mill note asks what happens when nobody challenges an accepted belief. Neither writer signed our watch slip.

options.text: Leave the rail ready.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The rail crew has a separate drum and can check the watch through two marks. That asks someone to be there before loading. A dated seal can let one crew use a test already carried out, as long as they know when it expires. Which direction shall we put on the first docket?

options.text: Start each shift with a rail comparison.
Use the dated repair record and its fallback.
Leave the docket open for now.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi sends a checker to the independent drum. The opening docket now asks for the first time and the next advancing minute. A match at one mark stays on the slip until the second mark completes the check.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi clips the seal and test date to the docket. A crew can use that shift’s signed result. If the seal breaks or the date is missing or old, the fallback sends someone to the independent rail for both marks.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: A courier came just as the shutter started to fall. There is a reply by the stair rail. Check what the courier can see and hear by the shutter.

options.text: Leave the rail ready.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The two crews are together for just a short part of the shift. Someone behind the shutter can miss one mark even when the check happens. Give that person a way to see or hear both readings before their hands fill with crates.

options.text: Set a spoken relay across the short overlap.
Put two large reference marks by the shutter.
Leave the first instruction ready.
I kept both landing sheets on the island.
I checked what someone could see from the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: You kept the original result when a loading condition changed. Our first check stays on its own docket too. The shutter changes how long people can share that check. Give the shorter overlap its own line.

options.text: Set a spoken relay across the short overlap.
Put two large reference marks by the shutter.
Leave the first instruction ready.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The lamps were clear from one approach and gone from another. Here the first call is clear at the rail and muffled beside the shutter. Give the person who starts there their own way to follow the two marks.

options.text: Set a spoken relay across the short overlap.
Put two large reference marks by the shutter.
Leave the first instruction ready.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi moves a second checker to the shutter before it falls. The rail checker calls both readings separately. The checker at the shutter repeats each one back for the waiting courier. The first docket stays signed.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi pins separate opening and next-minute marks where the courier can see them before lifting a crate. The first docket stays signed. Both marks point back to the independent drum.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: A new checker can use the marks and the dated docket. They have asked where the test came from if they need to check again after a long repair.

options.text: Leave a wide copy of the check instructions.
Keep the docket at the rail.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: Essi hangs the wider copy near the entrance. It leaves lines for who checked, which drum they used, and when. The dated first docket and its fallback stay with the repair slip.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The entrance copy tells a new checker where the original date and comparison belong. There is space for the next dated check beside it.

options.text: Leave the rail ready.
Find a place for the spare practice dial.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: One spare dial can go out before the shift starts. At the rail, an apprentice can stand with the crew and ask about the marks. Some people leave before handover. At the low slot, a person can stop with a cart and check with the keeper when they arrive.

options.text: Set the practice dial at the shared rail.
Set the practice dial in the low slot.
Leave the spare dial inside for now.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: The people at handover pass the dial along. An apprentice asks which reading came from the reference. The crew lead takes them back through the two marks before they go.

dialogue.speaker: council-reader
dialogue.text: A helper parks their cart beside the spare dial and turns it through the two marks. They missed handover, so the keeper shows them which mark to compare with the rail record.

cards.title: John Stuart Mill on challenge (1859)
cards.text: In chapter 2 of On Liberty, Mill argues that an accepted view can be true and still need a serious challenge. Encountering reasons and objections can help people understand the view they hold.
cards.limits: Mill’s argument concerns how people hold and discuss beliefs. It is separate from the Council’s fictional watch trial.

missions.title: When the Hand Moves
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What else needs to hold after a watch gives the right time once?

missions.title: A New Checker

objectives.title: Put a wide copy of the check near the entrance.

missions.title: A Dial for Handover
missions.knowledgeQuestion: Who gets a chance to see or question how a timing mark was made?

objectives.title: Check the crew’s handover and the low practice slot.
Place the spare dial and see who can use it.

journal.text: A stopped watch shared the drum’s first reading. Its next mark showed the limit of the match. Both loading crews now have a way to follow the check.

moments.did: You compared cases that agreed on the first mark and checked the next one.
moments.prompt: What does a second look show that the first match leaves open?

moments.did: You helped a courier on the other side of the shutter take part in the check.
moments.prompt: Where would you stand for both readings to be clear?

chronicle.title: The signed clock docket
chronicle.text: The loading crew has a way to check the watch. The docket names the separate drum or the dated repair test.

chronicle.title: Two marks at the shutter
chronicle.text: A courier needed both readings. The revised instruction gives the short overlap its own check while keeping the original docket.
